::: callout-note
## How to use this quiz

This quiz is designed as a **formative self-assessment tool**, not as a test.

Its purpose is to help you:
- check your understanding of the key concepts from Topic 3,
- identify which types of thinking you find more difficult, and
- guide your revision before the tutorial and future assessments.

### What this quiz measures

Each question belongs to one of four categories:

- **Subject Knowledge (SK):** definitions, concepts, and facts.  
- **Analysis (AN):** understanding relationships and economic mechanisms.  
- **Problem Solving (PS):** applying concepts to new situations.  
- **Mathematical Thinking (MT):** working with ratios, prices, and scaling.

Your score will be broken down by category so you can see **where** you are strong and where you need more practice.

### How to complete the quiz

- You may use your notes and the lecture materials.
- Take your time — the goal is understanding, not speed.
- Use the **Hints** if you get stuck.
- You may refresh and retry the quiz as many times as you like.

### How to interpret your results

- A low score is **not a problem** — it tells you what to focus on.
- If you score low in:
  - **SK:** revise definitions and core concepts.
  - **AN:** revisit the logic of the models and examples.
  - **PS:** practise applying concepts to new cases.
  - **MT:** practise the price and ratio calculations.

### About the leaderboard

The leaderboard is optional and anonymous. It exists only to make practice more engaging.  
It has **no effect** on your grade and is not used for evaluation.

The only purpose of this quiz is to support your learning.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(webexercises)
```

<!-- FEEDBACK SCRIPT: interactive quiz with self-assessment -->
```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  // 1) Configure your Google Apps Script Web App URL here.
  //    Example: https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXXXXXXXXXX/exec
  const ENDPOINT = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbysCOTW2ZLw5ruYY84Y-o0zB7nt0jkowiC3OoKJSdh2OYv-ZXa_1vTb_TU4BYwcwSZ0Jw/exec";

  const norm = s => (s || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

  function getSelectedLabelText(qEl) {
    const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
    if (!input) return "";
    const label = input.closest('label') || document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]');
    return label ? norm(label.textContent) : "";
  }

  function clearFeedback(qEl) {
    qEl.querySelectorAll("label").forEach(l => l.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect"));
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (line) {
      line.textContent = "";
      line.classList.add("hidden");
    }
  }

  function setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect) {
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (!line) return;
    line.textContent = isCorrect ? "Correct." : "Incorrect.";
    line.classList.remove("hidden");
  }

  async function postAttempt(payload) {
    // Do not attempt POST if ENDPOINT is not configured
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) return;

    try {
      await fetch(ENDPOINT, {
        method: "POST",
        mode: "no-cors",
        keepalive: true,
        body: JSON.stringify(payload)
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn("Could not save attempt:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadLeaderboard(quizName) {
    const table = document.getElementById("leaderboard");
    if (!table) return;

    // If not configured, show a friendly message and stop.
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Leaderboard is not configured yet. Add your Apps Script URL in the page source.</td></tr>";
      return;
    }

    try {
      const res = await fetch(ENDPOINT, { method: "GET" });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + res.status);
      const rows = await res.json();

      // Filter for this quiz only (defensive: older rows may not have the fields)
      const filtered = (rows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

      // Keep best score per nickname
      const best = new Map();
      filtered.forEach(r => {
        const nick = String(r.nickname || "").trim();
        if (!nick) return;
        const score = Number(r.score);
        const total = Number(r.total);
        const ts = new Date(r.timestamp || 0).getTime();

        const prev = best.get(nick);
        if (!prev || score > prev.score || (score === prev.score && ts < prev.ts)) {
          best.set(nick, { nickname: nick, score, total, ts });
        }
      });

      const leaderboard = Array.from(best.values())
        .sort((a, b) => (b.score - a.score) || (a.ts - b.ts))
        .slice(0, 30);

      if (leaderboard.length === 0) {
        table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>No attempts recorded yet.</td></tr>";
      } else {
        table.innerHTML =
          "<tr><th>Rank</th><th>Nickname</th><th>Score</th></tr>" +
          leaderboard.map((r, i) =>
            "<tr><td>" + (i + 1) + "</td><td>" + String(r.nickname) + "</td><td>" + r.score + " / " + r.total + "</td></tr>"
          ).join("");
      }

      // Load and display question statistics
      await loadQuestionStats(quizName, rows);
    } catch (err) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Could not load leaderboard.</td></tr>";
      console.warn("Leaderboard error:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadQuestionStats(quizName, allRows) {
    const statsContainer = document.getElementById("question-stats");
    if (!statsContainer) return;

    // Filter for this quiz only
    const filtered = (allRows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

    console.log("=== DEBUGGING QUESTION STATS ===");
    console.log("Filtered rows count:", filtered.length);
    if (filtered.length > 0) {
      console.log("Sample row:", filtered[0]);
    }

    // Build a map of question index to identifier
    const questionIdentifiers = {};
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)\)/);
      if (categoryMatch) {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];  // SK1, AN1, etc.
      } else {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = "Q" + (idx + 1);  // fallback
      }
    });

    console.log("Question identifiers map:", questionIdentifiers);

    // Count incorrect attempts per question
    const questionStats = {};
    filtered.forEach((row, rowIdx) => {
      let details = row.details || {};
      
      // If details is a string (JSON), parse it
      if (typeof details === 'string') {
        try {
          details = JSON.parse(details);
          console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Parsed details from string`);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn(`Row ${rowIdx} - Could not parse details:`, details);
          return;
        }
      }

      console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Processing details:`, details);

      Object.entries(details).forEach(([questionId, qData]) => {
        if (!questionStats[questionId]) {
          questionStats[questionId] = { incorrectCount: 0, totalCount: 0 };
        }
        
        questionStats[questionId].totalCount += 1;
        
        // Check if answer was incorrect (ok: 0 means incorrect)
        const isIncorrect = qData.ok === 0;
        if (isIncorrect) {
          questionStats[questionId].incorrectCount += 1;
        }
      });
    });

    console.log("\nFinal question stats:", questionStats);

    // Get top 10 most incorrect questions, sorted by incorrect count
    const sortedQuestions = Object.entries(questionStats)
      .map(([qKey, stats]) => ({
        qKey: qKey,  // Keep original identifier like SK1, AN1, Q1, etc.
        incorrectCount: stats.incorrectCount,
        totalCount: stats.totalCount,
        incorrectRate: stats.totalCount > 0 ? (stats.incorrectCount / stats.totalCount * 100).toFixed(1) : 0
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.incorrectCount - a.incorrectCount)
      .slice(0, 10);

    console.log("Sorted questions:", sortedQuestions);

    if (sortedQuestions.length === 0) {
      statsContainer.innerHTML = "<p>No question statistics available yet.</p>";
    } else {
      statsContainer.innerHTML =
        "<h4>Top 10 Questions with Most Incorrect Attempts</h4>" +
        "<table style='width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse;'>" +
        "<tr style='border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;'><th style='text-align: left; padding: 8px;'>Question</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Total Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Rate</th></tr>" +
        sortedQuestions.map(q =>
          "<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>" +
          "<td style='padding: 8px;'>" + String(q.qKey) + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.totalCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectRate + "%</td>" +
          "</tr>"
        ).join("") +
        "</table>";
    }
  }

  async function submitQuiz() {
    const nicknameEl = document.getElementById("nickname");
    const resultEl = document.getElementById("quiz-result");
    const submitBtn = document.getElementById("quiz-submit");

    const nickname = (nicknameEl?.value || "").trim();
    if (!nickname) {
      alert("Please enter a nickname before submitting.");
      nicknameEl?.focus();
      return;
    }

    // Lock submit to avoid double posting
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;

    let score = 0;
    let total = 0;
    const details = {};
    
    // Category scores
    const categories = {
      SK: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Subject Knowledge" },
      AN: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Analysis" },
      PS: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Problem Solving" },
      MT: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Mathematical Thinking" }
    };

    const questions = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q"));

    // Clear any prior feedback first (important if student re-submits)
    questions.forEach(clearFeedback);

    questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      total += 1;
      const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
      const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
      const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);

      const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
      if (isCorrect) score += 1;

      // Extract category and question ID from question text (SK1, AN1, PS1, MT1, etc.)
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)\)/);
      let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);  // fallback
      
      if (categoryMatch) {
        const cat = categoryMatch[1];
        const num = categoryMatch[2];
        questionId = cat + num;  // Use actual identifier like SK1, AN1, etc.
        
        categories[cat].total += 1;
        if (isCorrect) categories[cat].score += 1;
      }

      details[questionId] = { selected, correct, ok: isCorrect ? 1 : 0 };

      // Mark only after submit
      if (selected) {
        const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
        const label = input?.closest('label') || (input ? document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]') : null);
        if (label) label.classList.add(isCorrect ? "is-correct" : "is-incorrect");
      }
      setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect);
    });

    if (resultEl) {
      let resultHTML = "<strong>Overall Score: " + score + " / " + total + "</strong><br><br>";
      
      // Add category breakdown
      for (const key in categories) {
        const cat = categories[key];
        if (cat.total > 0) {
          resultHTML += cat.name + ": " + cat.score + " / " + cat.total + "<br>";
        }
      }
      
      // Add correct and incorrect questions
      const correctQuestions = [];
      const incorrectQuestions = [];
      
      questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
        const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
        const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
        const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);
        const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
        
        // Extract question ID from question text
        const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
        const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)\)/);
        let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);  // fallback
        if (categoryMatch) {
          questionId = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];  // SK1, AN1, etc.
        }
        
        if (selected) {
          if (isCorrect) {
            correctQuestions.push(questionId);
          } else {
            incorrectQuestions.push(questionId);
          }
        }
      });
      
      resultHTML += "<br><strong>Correct Questions:</strong> " + (correctQuestions.length > 0 ? correctQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      resultHTML += "<strong>Incorrect Questions:</strong> " + (incorrectQuestions.length > 0 ? incorrectQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      
      resultEl.innerHTML = resultHTML;
    }

    // Persist attempt (best practice: store what you need; nickname only = low GDPR footprint)
    await postAttempt({
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      nickname,
      quiz: "Topic3",
      score,
      total,
      details
    });

    // Refresh leaderboard after a successful submit (or best-effort submit)
    await loadLeaderboard("Topic3");

    // Disable all radio buttons and submit button to prevent further changes
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q input[type='radio']").forEach(input => {
      input.disabled = true;
    });
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;
  }

  // Expose submitQuiz globally for the button onclick
  window.submitQuiz = submitQuiz;

  // Add a feedback line container to each question if it doesn't exist
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach(qEl => {
      if (!qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line")) {
        const line = document.createElement("div");
        line.className = "quiz-feedback-line hidden";
        qEl.appendChild(line);
      }
    });

    loadLeaderboard("Topic3");
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Subject Knowledge

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK1) What does the Fisher equation relate?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Inflation and unemployment", answer = "Nominal interest rate, real interest rate, and inflation", "Output and interest rates", "Money growth and unemployment"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Nominal interest rate, real interest rate, and inflation"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recall the identity that decomposes nominal returns into real returns and expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK2) In the quantity theory of money, velocity refers to:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("The growth rate of output", answer = "The number of times money changes hands in a period", "The interest rate set by the central bank", "The inflation rate"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The number of times money changes hands in a period"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think about how frequently a unit of currency is used in transactions.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK3) If money is neutral in the long run, a permanent increase in money growth affects:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Real output permanently", "Real interest rates permanently", answer = "Nominal variables but not real variables", "Unemployment permanently"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Nominal variables but not real variables"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Distinguish between nominal and real variables when considering long-run neutrality.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK4) Expected inflation primarily affects:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("The real interest rate directly", answer = "The nominal interest rate via the Fisher effect", "Productivity growth", "Government spending"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The nominal interest rate via the Fisher effect"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the relationship between expected inflation and nominal returns.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK5) Superneutrality of money implies that a change in money growth affects:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "Inflation but not real variables", "Real output growth", "The natural rate of unemployment", "Productivity"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation but not real variables"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Superneutrality strengthens neutrality by extending it to growth rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK6) In a Taylor rule framework, the central bank responds systematically to:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Money supply shocks only", answer = "Deviations of inflation and output from targets", "Fiscal deficits", "Exchange rates only"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Deviations of inflation and output from targets"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think of the two main gaps policymakers typically stabilise.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK7) A rise in expected inflation, holding the real rate constant, will:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Lower the nominal interest rate", answer = "Raise the nominal interest rate one-for-one", "Leave the nominal rate unchanged", "Reduce velocity"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Raise the nominal interest rate one-for-one"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the Fisher equation mechanically.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK8) If velocity is unstable, a constant money growth rule may:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Stabilise output perfectly", answer = "Lead to fluctuations in nominal income", "Fix inflation exactly", "Eliminate business cycles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Lead to fluctuations in nominal income"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Recall the quantity equation and what happens if one component varies unpredictably.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK9) In the long run under classical assumptions, inflation is primarily determined by:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Productivity growth", "Fiscal policy", answer = "Money growth", "Labour supply"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Money growth"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider the proportional relationship implied by the quantity theory.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK10) If the central bank increases money growth permanently, the Fisher effect predicts that in the long run:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Real rates rise permanently", answer = "Nominal rates rise with inflation", "Real output rises permanently", "Velocity becomes constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Nominal rates rise with inflation"></span>

## Analysis

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN1) If expected inflation rises but the nominal rate does not adjust immediately, what happens to the real rate?**

<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>

## Problem Solving

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS1) A country doubles its money supply while velocity and output remain constant. What happens to prices?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("They halve", answer = "They double", "They stay constant", "They fall slightly"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="They double"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use proportional reasoning from MV = PY.</details>

</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS8) A credible disinflation reduces expected inflation by 3 percentage points. If the real rate is unchanged, nominal rates will:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Rise by 3", answer = "Fall by 3", "Stay constant", "Double"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Fall by 3"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the Fisher relationship symmetrically.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS9) If output exceeds potential and inflation is above target, a Taylor rule implies:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Lower rates", answer = "Higher rates", "Money growth targeting", "Fiscal expansion"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Higher rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider both inflation and output gaps.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS10) If money growth exceeds real growth persistently, long-run inflation will:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Be negative", answer = "Equal money growth minus real growth", "Equal real growth", "Be zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Equal money growth minus real growth"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Rearrange the steady-state quantity equation.</details>
</div>

## Mathematical Thinking

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT1) If nominal rate is 5% and expected inflation is 2%, the real rate is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "3%", "7%", "2%", "-3%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="3%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Real rate is approximately nominal minus expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT2) Money growth is 8%, real growth is 3%, velocity constant. Inflation is approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("11%", answer = "5%", "3%", "8%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="5%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use steady-state approximation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT3) If MV = PY and M grows 4%, V constant, Y grows 1%, inflation is approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "3%", "4%", "1%", "5%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="3%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Subtract real growth from money growth.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT4) Nominal rate 9%, expected inflation 6%. Real rate:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("15%", answer = "3%", "-3%", "6%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="3%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply Fisher equation directly.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT5) Money growth increases by 2 percentage points permanently. In the long run, inflation:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Falls", answer = "Rises by 2 points", "Rises by 1 point", "Unchanged"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Rises by 2 points"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Assume neutrality and constant real growth.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT6) Velocity growth is 3%, money growth is 5%, real growth is 4%. Inflation is approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "4%", "8%", "1%", "2%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="4%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Combine money and velocity growth, then subtract real growth.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT7) Expected inflation rises from 2% to 5%, real rate constant at 2%. Nominal rate becomes:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("4%", answer = "7%", "3%", "5%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="7%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Add real rate to new expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT8) Money growth 10%, velocity growth -2%, real growth 3%. Inflation is approximately:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "5%", "9%", "15%", "11%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="5%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Net nominal growth equals money plus velocity growth.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT9) If nominal rate is 12% and real rate is 4%, expected inflation is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("16%", answer = "8%", "4%", "-8%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="8%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Rearrange the Fisher equation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT10) Money growth equals real growth. Velocity constant. Inflation is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Positive", answer = "Zero", "Negative", "Equal to money growth"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Zero"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>When nominal income and real output grow equally, prices are stable.</details>
</div>
